text.title: django-quality Core Rules
text.summary: Eight rules for the Django quality toolchain.

rule.statement: `ruff` replaces `black`, `isort`, `flake8`, `pyupgrade`, `pydocstyle`. There is no `setup.cfg`, no `.flake8`, no `pyproject.toml` `[tool.black]` block. Single source of truth: `[tool.ruff]`.
rule.rationale: ruff is 10-100x faster and consolidates the toolchain. Running multiple formatters concurrently produces conflicting fixes and slow pre-commit runs.

rule.statement: `mypy --strict` runs in CI with `plugins = ["mypy_django_plugin.main"]`. `django-stubs` and `djangorestframework-stubs` installed. Per-module overrides for `tests.*` and `migrations.*`.
rule.rationale: Without the django plugin, every `.objects.filter()` is `Any`. With it, the entire ORM is statically typed.

rule.statement: `bandit -r apps/ -ll` runs in CI, scoped to high-severity findings. Allowlist any findings explicitly in `.bandit` or `# nosec` comments with justification.
rule.rationale: Bandit catches `eval`, hard-coded secrets, weak crypto, shell injection. Low-severity findings are too noisy for a gate; high-severity only.

rule.statement: `pre-commit` runs ruff (format + check), mypy, bandit, djlint, and a `check-migrations` hook. Configuration in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
rule.rationale: Pre-commit centralises hooks across editors and CI. Without it, hooks drift between developer machines.

rule.statement: All tool config in `pyproject.toml`. No `setup.cfg`, no `.flake8`, no `.isort.cfg`, no `pytest.ini`. One file = one source of truth.
rule.rationale: Scattered config produces silent overrides and broken IDE pickup.

rule.statement: When the project is Django 5.x or 4.2 LTS on Python 3.12+, the code lives under `apps/<app>/` or `core/`, `pytest + pytest-django` is configured and service-layer separation is agreed, the toolchain audit MUST run on a named trigger - any change to a `[tool.*]` table in `pyproject.toml`, a new `apps/<app>/`, or the CI `pre-commit run --all-files` job - and MUST produce the 02-output-contract record from the configuration itself: `formatter` and `linter` from `[tool.ruff]`, `type_checker` and `django_stubs_plugin` from `[tool.mypy]` carrying `plugins = ["mypy_django_plugin.main"]`, `security_scanner` from the `bandit -r apps/ -ll` hook, `pre_commit_used` from `.pre-commit-config.yaml` listing ruff, mypy, bandit, djlint and `check-migrations`, and `config_consolidated` from a scan proving no `setup.cfg`, `.flake8`, `.isort.cfg` or `pytest.ini` exists.

rationale.source: ruff docs; pre-commit docs; django-stubs docs

rule.rationale: Every field of the record is a constant, so a record typed from memory can only be right. Reading the tables and hook list is what makes fm-01 (black beside ruff) and fm-02 (mypy without the plugin) fail as a field instead of surviving as a slow pre-commit and an `Any`-typed ORM.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but a required field cannot be computed - `pyproject.toml` has no `[tool.ruff]` table, `.pre-commit-config.yaml` is absent so `pre_commit_used` cannot be read, `apps/` does not exist so `bandit -r apps/` has no target, or `[tool.mypy]` is present but `django-stubs` is not installed so `django_stubs_plugin` is undecidable - the audit MUST block naming the missing file or table from the Prerequisites, and MUST NOT emit a record claiming `config_consolidated: true` while `setup.cfg` or `.flake8` still exist, or `type_checker: mypy` without the plugin line.
rule.rationale: A `setup.cfg` left beside `pyproject.toml` silently overrides the ruff and pytest tables in some tools and not others (fm-05); a record that says consolidated while it exists reports the exact configuration the rule forbids as compliant. Blocking on the named file costs a minute; the silent override costs a release.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - the project is not Django (FastAPI, Flask), it is a throwaway tool with no growth horizon, or the `apps/core/config` layout is not adopted and refactoring it is out of scope - the methodology MUST NOT be applied; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor (the `pyproject.toml` commit or the ticket) naming the failed precondition and the route taken instead (`python-typing` for the checker baseline on non-Django Python; `django-coding-standards` first when the layout is the blocker), and a legacy `black + flake8` stack MUST NOT be filed as a partial pass of this methodology.
rule.rationale: ruff and bandit run on any Python tree, so the temptation is to record a half-applied toolchain on a project outside the preconditions and count it. The anchored skip keeps the record honest: the layout refactor comes first, and the audit reopens on the commit that lands it.
